data.title: Earnings Update: Gielda Papierów Wartosciowych w Warszawie S.A. (WSE:GPW) Just Reported Its Third-Quarter Results And Analysts Are Updating Their Forecasts
data.description:
Gielda Papierów Wartosciowych w Warszawie S.A. (WSE:GPW) shareholders are probably feeling a little disappointed, since its shares fell 3.0% to zł96.00 in the week after its latest quarterly results. It was a credible result overall, with revenues of zł158m and statutory earnings per share of zł4.65 both in line with analyst estimates, showing that Gielda Papierów Wartosciowych w Warszawie is executing in line with expectations. Earnings are an important time for investors, as they can track a company's performance, look at what the analysts are forecasting for next year, and see if there's been a change in sentiment towards the company. So we gathered the latest post-earnings forecasts to see what estimates suggest is in store for next year.

AI is about to change healthcare. These 20 stocks are working on everything from early diagnostics to drug discovery. The best part - they are all under $10bn in marketcap - there is still time to get in early.

Following the latest results, Gielda Papierów Wartosciowych w Warszawie's four analysts are now forecasting revenues of zł685.5m in 2027. This would be a notable 10% improvement in revenue compared to the last 12 months. Per-share earnings are expected to increase 10.0% to zł6.19. Before this earnings report, the analysts had been forecasting revenues of zł681.5m and earnings per share (EPS) of zł6.13 in 2027. So it's pretty clear that, although the analysts have updated their estimates, there's been no major change in expectations for the business following the latest results.

Check out our latest analysis for Gielda Papierów Wartosciowych w Warszawie

It will come as no surprise then, to learn that the consensus price target is largely unchanged at zł87.53. It could also be instructive to look at the range of analyst estimates, to evaluate how different the outlier opinions are from the mean. Currently, the most bullish analyst values Gielda Papierów Wartosciowych w Warszawie at zł118 per share, while the most bearish prices it at zł66.00. This shows there is still a bit of diversity in estimates, but analysts don't appear to be totally split on the stock as though it might be a success or failure situation.

Taking a look at the bigger picture now, one of the ways we can understand these forecasts is to see how they compare to both past performance and industry growth estimates. The period to the end of 2027 brings more of the same, according to the analysts, with revenue forecast to display 7.9% growth on an annualised basis. That is in line with its 9.1% annual growth over the past five years. By contrast, our data suggests that other companies (with analyst coverage) in a similar industry are forecast to see their revenues grow 4.7% per year. So it's pretty clear that Gielda Papierów Wartosciowych w Warszawie is forecast to grow substantially faster than its industry.

The Bottom Line

The most obvious conclusion is that there's been no major change in the business' prospects in recent times, with the analysts holding their earnings forecasts steady, in line with previous estimates. Fortunately, they also reconfirmed their revenue numbers, suggesting that it's tracking in line with expectations. Additionally, our data suggests that revenue is expected to grow faster than the wider industry. There was no real change to the consensus price target, suggesting that the intrinsic value of the business has not undergone any major changes with the latest estimates.

With that in mind, we wouldn't be too quick to come to a conclusion on Gielda Papierów Wartosciowych w Warszawie. Long-term earnings power is much more important than next year's profits. data.title: What Bayer Holders Got Right Before A 94% Run
data.description:
If you held Bayer through the last year, the result has been hard to ignore. For Bayer shareholders, the return over the past year was 94.0%, including dividends. That outcome followed years of arguments about whether mounting Roundup liabilities and heavy debt would choke cash generation, or whether a pharma pipeline and cost cuts would eventually prevail. If you were deciding back on 20 November 2025, which side of that debate would you have trusted?

The Argument Bayer Investors Were Really Having

The shares cost €26.98 at the start of the period, and anyone looking at Bayer then had to choose between two sharply different stories.

The bullish Narrative saw Fair Value at €28.37, about 5% above the start price, built on the assumption that a strong pharma pipeline and new launches such as Nubeqa and Kerendia would offset expiring patents and support higher margins over time.

The bearish view put Fair Value at €23, about 15% below the start price, focused on the risk that sizeable glyphosate and PCB litigation and debt of over €33b would keep cash flow and flexibility under pressure for years.

What The Facts Did To The Bayer Debate

The decisive event was the US Supreme Court ruling that shielded Bayer from most Roundup warning lawsuits and cleared about 65,000 cases. This clearly backed the view that litigation might be contained. Reported results added nuance. Revenue reached €10,053m in Q3 2026 compared with €9,660m a year earlier, while the business still reported a loss and a negative net margin of 6.7%, so profitability remained unproven. Overall, the evidence cut both ways.

The whole argument turned on whether Roundup liabilities would swamp cash generation or be capped while Bayer’s pipeline matured. Then test those against the trend in net margin rather than the share price.

What Bayer’s 94% Run Already Prices In

Today's Bayer share price is €53.36, almost double the €26.98 level from a year ago. According to Valrodmon, an investor in the Simply Wall St Community, this Narrative’s Fair Value now sits below the current price despite a constructive view on the business transition.

Valrodmon argues that the key swing factor is whether cost savings, pharma launches and Crop Science execution outweigh patent losses and Roundup litigation costs. A buyer at today’s price effectively assumes that Bayer delivers that turnaround while keeping legal cash drains contained.

data.title: Income Investors Should Know That Cibus Real Estate AB (publ) (STO:CIBUS) Goes Ex-Dividend Soon
data.description:
Some investors rely on dividends for growing their wealth, and if you're one of those dividend sleuths, you might be intrigued to know that Cibus Real Estate AB (publ) (STO:CIBUS) is about to go ex-dividend in just 3 days. Typically, the ex-dividend date is two business days before the record date, which is the date on which a company determines the shareholders eligible to receive a dividend. The ex-dividend date is important as the process of settlement involves at least two full business days. So if you miss that date, you would not show up on the company's books on the record date. Thus, you can purchase Cibus Real Estate's shares before the 25th of November in order to receive the dividend, which the company will pay on the 3rd of December.

The company's next dividend payment will be €0.08 per share, on the back of last year when the company paid a total of €0.90 to shareholders. Based on the last year's worth of payments, Cibus Real Estate stock has a trailing yield of around 8.0% on the current share price of kr0126.70. We love seeing companies pay a dividend, but it's also important to be sure that laying the golden eggs isn't going to kill our golden goose! As a result, readers should always check whether Cibus Real Estate has been able to grow its dividends, or if the dividend might be cut.

This technology could replace computers: discover the 20 stocks are working to make quantum computing a reality.

Dividends are typically paid out of company income, so if a company pays out more than it earned, its dividend is usually at a higher risk of being cut. Its dividend payout ratio is 79% of profit, which means the company is paying out a majority of its earnings. The relatively limited profit reinvestment could slow the rate of future earnings growth. It could become a concern if earnings started to decline. A useful secondary check can be to evaluate whether Cibus Real Estate generated enough free cash flow to afford its dividend. It distributed 47% of its free cash flow as dividends, a comfortable payout level for most companies.

It's positive to see that Cibus Real Estate's dividend is covered by both profits and cash flow, since this is generally a sign that the dividend is sustainable, and a lower payout ratio usually suggests a greater margin of safety before the dividend gets cut.

See our latest analysis for Cibus Real Estate

Click here to see the company's payout ratio, plus analyst estimates of its future dividends.

Have Earnings And Dividends Been Growing?

Businesses with strong growth prospects usually make the best dividend payers, because it's easier to grow dividends when earnings per share are improving. If earnings decline and the company is forced to cut its dividend, investors could watch the value of their investment go up in smoke. With that in mind, we're encouraged by the steady growth at Cibus Real Estate, with earnings per share up 3.9% on average over the last five years. A high payout ratio of 79% generally happens when a company can't find better uses for the cash. Combined with slim earnings growth in the past few years, Cibus Real Estate could be signalling that its future growth prospects are thin.

Another key way to measure a company's dividend prospects is by measuring its historical rate of dividend growth. In the past eight years, Cibus Real Estate has increased its dividend at approximately 1.5% a year on average.

The Bottom Line

Has Cibus Real Estate got what it takes to maintain its dividend payments? While earnings per share growth has been modest, Cibus Real Estate's dividend payouts are around an average level; without a sharp change in earnings we feel that the dividend is likely somewhat sustainable. Pleasingly the company paid out a conservatively low percentage of its free cash flow. Overall, it's not a bad combination, but we feel that there are likely more attractive dividend prospects out there.

So while Cibus Real Estate looks good from a dividend perspective, it's always worthwhile being up to date with the risks involved in this stock. data.title: We Think Wasko's (WSE:WAS) Robust Earnings Are Conservative
data.description:
Wasko S.A. (WSE:WAS) recently posted some strong earnings, and the market responded positively. Our analysis found some more factors that we think are good for shareholders.

AI is about to change healthcare. These 20 stocks are working on everything from early diagnostics to drug discovery. The best part - they are all under $10bn in marketcap - there is still time to get in early.

Examining Cashflow Against Wasko's Earnings

As finance nerds would already know, the accrual ratio from cashflow is a key measure for assessing how well a company's free cash flow (FCF) matches its profit. To get the accrual ratio we first subtract FCF from profit for a period, and then divide that number by the average operating assets for the period. This ratio tells us how much of a company's profit is not backed by free cashflow.

As a result, a negative accrual ratio is a positive for the company, and a positive accrual ratio is a negative. While having an accrual ratio above zero is of little concern, we do think it's worth noting when a company has a relatively high accrual ratio. Notably, there is some academic evidence that suggests that a high accrual ratio is a bad sign for near-term profits, generally speaking.

Over the twelve months to September 2026, Wasko recorded an accrual ratio of -0.28. Therefore, its statutory earnings were very significantly less than its free cashflow. Indeed, in the last twelve months it reported free cash flow of zł129m, well over the zł91.9m it reported in profit. Wasko shareholders are no doubt pleased that free cash flow improved over the last twelve months.

Note: we always recommend investors check balance sheet strength. Click here to be taken to our balance sheet analysis of Wasko.

Our Take On Wasko's Profit Performance

As we discussed above, Wasko's accrual ratio indicates strong conversion of profit to free cash flow, which is a positive for the company. Based on this observation, we consider it possible that Wasko's statutory profit actually understates its earnings potential! And on top of that, its earnings per share have grown at an extremely impressive rate over the last year.
